pages.text: Every old stone village you find is dead. Learn the rule early: $(bold)old stone means dead; a tower means people$().$(br2)Most are $(bold)abandoned$(): roofs open, glass gone, the dead owners still in the cellars, a little left in the chests and sometimes a journal. The rest are $(bold)held$(): pillagers camp in them, and the chests hold what they took from every town they emptied.

An abandoned village is a quarry, a shelter and a story. A held one is a fight with real loot at the end. Neither has a bell that works, a board that posts, or a villager who trades.$(br2)Cure the zombie villagers, or bring villagers of your own, put down a recruit table and ring a bell: the survivors will found a new town on the old bones ($(l:patchouli:towns/new_towns)The New Towns$()).

A few old towns live on, far apart. The nearest is the $(bold)capital$(), where you woke. It is neutral ground: no faction can take it or found one in it. Raids are its only threat, and the moment you are needed.$(br2)Smaller things litter the land between: fallen logs, cairns, a derailed cart, a platform where the morning engine never came. Read them. They are the same story told in blocks.
